purpose: Compare the strongest currently accessible real-world pairing for Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode, with Qwen3.8-27B retained as the smaller open-model efficiency control and Fable 5 preserved as an explicit access limitation.

supersedes.reason: The first shared-harness block exposed a naming-dependent private CSS assertion before the top-native block began. This protocol uses a separately versioned task and behavior-focused browser QA while preserving the original protocol and raw results.

route_resolution.requested_route_result: Recognized by Claude Code but returned HTTP 429 before inference because usage credits are not enabled.
route_resolution.label: best accessible Claude route; not a Fable substitute
route_resolution.future_fable_policy: If usage credits are enabled later, run Fable 5 only in a separately preregistered addendum.

baseline.resolution: Use the clean Git commit containing this preregistration file for every run. The exact commit is captured independently in each run manifest.

access_preconditions: Use the completed tiny generic access checks recorded in benchmark/access/T4-top-native-v2-access-checks.json; no checked model saw the benchmark task.
Keep the combined Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8-27B access-check and counted-run spend at or below the user-approved $1.50 OpenRouter ceiling.
Do not call Fable 5 again in this block because the pre-freeze check established that usage credits are disabled.
Do not increase an account or API spending limit.
If an exact route is unavailable, record an access limitation and do not silently substitute another model inside this block.

external_browser_qa: initial render, visible outcome text, and summaries
keyboard focus and visible focus style
desktop and 390 px layouts without horizontal page overflow

rules: Execute in the preregistered order without substituting a route.
Use a fresh isolated worktree and session for every run.
Preserve failures, partial outputs, provider errors, and access limitations as results.
Do not rerun a failed route inside this pilot block.
Run the same external browser-QA checklist against every reconstructed patch.
Keep subscription access separate from metered API cost.
Do not claim a general winner from one run per route.
